title: Impact
meta_description: What Sounds of Saving has done so far: films with artists, programs in schools, resources at shows, and the research behind it.
heading: What we've done so far
lead: We keep this page honest. These are the numbers and moments we can stand behind today; it grows as the work does.

stats.label: Song That Found Me at the Right Time sessions filmed with artists, in partnership with the 988 Lifeline since 2022
NYC public high schools reached in 2023 through MTV's Mental Health Action Day, the programs that became SoS HS
sessions in the SoS HS program, now piloting in Washington, DC and evaluated with NYU's Ripollés Lab
vetted mental-health resources in our Get Help directory, shared at shows on wallet cards and available online

milestones.body: Sounds of Saving starts as a nonprofit studio making films with artists about coping and mental health.
Charlie Gross joins Nick Greto as co-founder, bringing a clinician's perspective to the work.
The national Lifeline becomes 988. Song That Found Me at the Right Time is produced in partnership with it from here on.
First school programs in two NYC public high schools. Tables at Re:SET, The National's Homecoming, and 6LACK's Since I Have a Lover tour.
The Secretary of Education shares his Songs That Found Me playlist for Mental Health Awareness Month. NYU's Pablo Ripollés joins the advisory board.
A Sound Approach, our research paper with NYU and the We Are All Music Foundation. Named to City & State's Responsible 100.
SoS HS pilots in Washington, DC. Program visits to Montclair Kimberley Academy and Hollywood High School.

testimonial.body: A principal told us that a high-risk student who had rejected every counseling outreach said this about the program. For us it was the whole thesis proven: music-based programming reaches students who are falling through the cracks.
